## Revelation 13: Verse-by-Verse Commentary Notes

### v. 1: *"Then I saw a beast with ten horns and seven heads rising out of the sea. There were ten royal crowns on its horns and blasphemous names on its heads."*

- **The sea** represents the Gentile nations — chaotic, restless, resisting God (cf. Dan. 7:2‑3; Rev. 17:15). The beast arises from the Gentile world. The Jewish people regarded the sea as a place of evil and chaos. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/; https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **The beast (θηρίον)** is a wild, dangerous animal — distinct from the dragon (Satan, Rev. 12:9), yet closely identified with him. He has the same seven heads and ten horns as the dragon (Rev. 12:3). This is the figure commonly known as the Antichrist. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **Seven heads** = seven world kingdoms (identified in Rev. 17:9‑10 as "seven mountains… seven kings"). Five had fallen by John's day; one "is" (Rome); the seventh "has not yet come." The beast is the seventh head that receives a mortal wound and revives as an "eighth." (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **Ten horns** = ten kings who rule contemporaneously with the beast (Rev. 17:12‑13). They give their power to him. This echoes Daniel 7:7, 24. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary; https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **Ten crowns on the horns** (not on the heads, as with the dragon): these crowns (διαδήματα, royal crowns) indicate the sovereign rule of the ten kings. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/; https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **Blasphemous names** on the heads: the beast's character is blasphemy. This echoes Daniel 11:36 — the willful king who "exalts and magnifies himself above every god." The Pulpit Commentary notes that worldly power denies the true God and exalts itself above Him, as seen partially in Pharaoh, Sennacherib, and Roman emperors who claimed divine titles. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/13-1.htm; https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **Gill's Exposition** identifies the first beast as the Romish antichrist in his **civil power**, the second beast (v. 11) as his ecclesiastical power. (https://www.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/13.htm)
- **MacArthur (Baptist/dispensational)**: This is the most graphic presentation of the Antichrist anywhere in Scripture. He is a real, future individual — Satan's false Christ. (https://www.gty.org/sermons/66-44/the-beast-out-of-the-sea-part-1)

---

### v. 2: *"The beast I saw was like a leopard, with the feet of a bear and the mouth of a lion. And the dragon gave the beast his power and his throne and great authority."*

- **Leopard, bear, lion**: composite of Daniel 7's first three beasts — Babylon (lion), Medo‑Persia (bear), Greece (leopard). This final beast combines their characteristics and embodies Daniel's fourth terrible beast (Rome / final world empire). The order is reversed from Daniel because John writes from a later vantage point. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/; https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **The dragon gave him his power, throne, and great authority**: The beast is directly empowered by Satan — described as "energized" by Satan (2 Thess. 2:9). The beast accepts the very offer Jesus refused in the temptation (Matt. 4:8‑10). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/; https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- This is the "incarnation of the Devil" — Satan's parody of the God‑Man. All the malignity, cunning, and power of the Serpent will be embodied in this man. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **Is the beast a man or an empire?** Precept Austin argues it is **both**: the beast is a man (masculine pronoun in v. 8; his number is "a man's number"; he receives worship; he goes to perdition personally — Rev. 19:20), yet he is inseparably united with the empire he leads. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **MacArthur**: The Antichrist is a human being, demon‑possessed by a spirit from the abyss; the ultimate wicked dictator, Satan's man. He rises from a confederacy of ten nations. (https://www.gty.org/sermons/66-44/the-beast-out-of-the-sea-part-1)
- **Ellicott**: The beast is the vicegerent of the dragon; through this succession of world‑powers the dragon carries on his war. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/13.htm)

---

### v. 3: *"One of the heads of the beast appeared to be mortally wounded. But the mortal wound was healed, and the whole world marveled and followed the beast."*

- The wound is on **one of the seven heads** — identified with the seventh head (the beast kingdom not yet come in John's day). The healed head becomes "the eighth" (Rev. 17:11). (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- This is a **mortal (deadly) wound**, not superficial. The beast's recovery is a **Satanic counterfeit of Christ's death and resurrection**. The world marvels and follows him precisely because of this healing. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **Some who see the beast as a government** (not a man) interpret this as the revival of the Roman Empire. Yet the most natural reading sees a person who dies and is healed. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **Precept Austin** rules out Nero as the beast because the world's worship comes **after** the healing — people would not worship a failed legend who died by suicide. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)

---

### v. 4: *"They worshiped the dragon who had given authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, 'Who is like the beast, and who can wage war against it?'"*

- The world worships **both** the dragon and the beast. Worship of the dragon may be **unknowing** — they think they worship the beast, but ultimately it goes to Satan. Satan appears as an angel of light (2 Cor. 11:14‑15). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- The cry "Who is like the beast?" is a blasphemous parody of worship of God (cf. Exod. 15:11, "Who is like You, O LORD?"). (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/13-4.htm)
- **Worship is justified purely on the ground of brute force** — because of the beast's apparent invincibility. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- Precept Austin notes this worship is directly linked to the healing of the mortal wound — the catalyst for worldwide adoration. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)

---

### v. 5: *"The beast was given a mouth to speak arrogant and blasphemous words, and authority to act for 42 months."*

- **42 months** = three and a half years — the familiar half‑week of Daniel's seventy weeks (Dan. 9:27). This is the duration of the beast's unrestrained reign in the **first half** of the final seven‑year tribulation (or the second half, depending on one's eschatological scheme). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- The beast's authority is **given** (passive) — he operates only within God's sovereign permission. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- The beast is characterized by **arrogant, blasphemous speech** — matching Daniel's "little horn" who speaks against the Most High (Dan. 7:25). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)

---

### v. 6: *"And the beast opened its mouth to speak blasphemies against God and to slander His name and His tabernacle—those who dwell in heaven."*

- The beast blasphemes **God's name, His tabernacle, and those who dwell in heaven**. "Those who dwell in heaven" may refer to the saints taken in the rapture — now out of his reach, so he can only blaspheme them. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- This is a direct assault on everything associated with God. "Blasphemer" may be an even more fitting title than "Antichrist." (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)

---

### v. 7: *"Then the beast was permitted to wage war against the saints and to conquer them, and it was given authority over every tribe and people and tongue and nation."*

- The beast is **permitted** (again passive — God's sovereign permission) to make war on the saints. He "conquers" them — meaning he can **kill their bodies**, not defeat their faith. He appears to defeat God's cause on earth. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **Who are these saints?** Pre‑tribulation interpreters say these are people saved **after** the church is raptured (tribulation saints). Post‑trib interpreters see the church itself. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- The beast has **worldwide authority** — over every tribe, tongue, and nation. This is a truly global dictatorship. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **MacArthur**: The Antichrist's agenda is to destroy Israel (so God's promises cannot be fulfilled), to prevent Gentile salvation, and to kill all who believe. (https://www.gty.org/sermons/66-44/the-beast-out-of-the-sea-part-1)

---

### v. 8: *"And all who dwell on the earth will worship the beast—all whose names have not been written from the foundation of the world in the Book of Life belonging to the Lamb who was slain."*

- **Worship of the beast and having your name in the Book of Life are mutually exclusive.** The beast receives universal worship from the reprobate. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **"The Lamb slain from the foundation of the world"**: God's plan of redemption was set before creation. This title emphasizes that history is unfolding according to God's eternal decree. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- The masculine pronoun "him" (αὐτόν) is used for the neuter "beast" (θηρίον), indicating the beast is a **human person**, not merely a system. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **Gill**: Only the reprobate part of the world worships the beast — those not elect, whose names are absent from the Lamb's Book of Life. (https://www.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/13.htm)

---

### vv. 9‑10: *"'He who has an ear, let him hear: If anyone is destined for captivity, into captivity he will go; if anyone is to die by the sword, by the sword he must be killed.' Here is a call for the perseverance and faith of the saints."*

- **"He who has an ear, let him hear"** — a solemn call to pay close attention, used throughout Revelation for spiritual comprehension. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- The warning means the functionaries of the beast are **not without guilt** — though these events are prophesied, personal responsibility remains. If you lead others into captivity, you will go into captivity; God will measure back what you measured to others. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- An alternative or additional meaning: **there is no hope in fighting the Antichrist by force**; the only path to victory is steadfast faith and endurance. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- "Here is the patience and faith of the saints" — though viciously attacked, the saints must trust in God's ultimate justice. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)

---

### v. 11: *"Then I saw another beast rising out of the earth. This beast had two horns like a lamb, but spoke like a dragon."*

- **The second beast** is distinct from the first: different in origin (earth vs. sea), rank (subordinate — causes worship of the first beast), and appearance (lamb‑like). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- He is called the **False Prophet** (Rev. 16:13; 19:20; 20:10). Together with the dragon and the first beast, they form an **"unholy trinity"**: Satan (anti‑Father), Antichrist (anti‑Christ), False Prophet (anti‑Holy Spirit). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **Two horns like a lamb**: a mild, harmless appearance — a counterfeit of Christ the Lamb. Yet he **speaks like a dragon** — his message is Satanic. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **Rising from the earth/land**: some see this as a clue the False Prophet is Jewish in origin — "the earth" sometimes means "the land" (of Israel) in Revelation. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **MacArthur**: The Antichrist is primarily political/military; the False Prophet is the **religious leader** who promotes worship of the Antichrist. Political power joined with religious power. (https://www.gty.org/sermons/66-47/the-final-false-prophet-part-1)

---

### v. 12: *"And this beast exercised all the authority of the first beast and caused the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast, whose mortal wound had been healed."*

- The second beast exercises **all the authority** of the first — he is the Antichrist's chief agent. His primary role is to direct worship to the first beast. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- The healed mortal wound is again mentioned — this is the central propaganda point driving the world's worship. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)

---

### v. 13: *"And the second beast performed great signs to cause even fire from heaven to come down to earth in the presence of the people."*

- The False Prophet performs **genuine supernatural signs** — not mere trickery. Even demonic spirits perform signs (Rev. 16:14). Fire from heaven mimics Elijah's miracle (1 Kings 18) and the two witnesses (Rev. 11:5). (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- This is the working of Satan "with all power, signs, and lying wonders" (2 Thess. 2:9). The signs are bona fide but what they attest is **false**. God also sends "strong delusion" so that unbelievers believe the lie (2 Thess. 2:11‑12). (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **Warning**: signs are unreliable indicators of a work of God. Jesus warned that many will say, "Lord, have we not done many wonders in Your name?" and He will reply, "I never knew you" (Matt. 7:22‑23). (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)

---

### v. 14: *"Because of the signs it was given to perform on behalf of the first beast, it deceived those who dwell on the earth, telling them to make an image to the beast that had been wounded by the sword and yet had lived."*

- The signs are **"on behalf of"** the first beast — they authenticate the Antichrist's claims and deceive the world. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- The image of the beast echoes **Daniel 3** (Nebuchadnezzar's golden image) — a global demand for idolatrous worship, enforced by death. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)

---

### v. 15: *"The second beast was permitted to give breath to the image of the first beast, so that the image could speak and cause all who refused to worship it to be killed."*

- The False Prophet **animates the image** — whether this is a demonic miracle, technological illusion, or something else, the image appears alive and speaks. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **Death penalty** for those who refuse to worship. This is the ultimate enforcement of the beast's religious system. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)

---

### vv. 16‑17: *"And the second beast required all people small and great, rich and poor, free and slave, to receive a mark on their right hand or on their forehead, so that no one could buy or sell unless he had the mark—the name of the beast or the number of its name."*

- **The mark of the beast**: a mark on the right hand or forehead, without which no one can participate in the economy (buy or sell). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- The mark mirrors the **seal of God** on the foreheads of His servants (Rev. 7:3; 14:1) — a Satanic counterfeit. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- The mark is specifically tied to the **name or number** of the beast — a declaration of allegiance. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)
- **All social classes** are affected: small and great, rich and poor, free and slave — no one is exempt. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/)

---

### v. 18: *"Here is a call for wisdom: Let the one who has insight calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man, and that number is 666."*

- **Traditional (gematria) interpretation**: In both Hebrew and Greek, letters had numerical values. The name "Neron Caesar" in Hebrew letters sums to 666. This is the most common identification in older commentaries (e.g., D.S. Clark on StudyLight). Some early manuscripts read 616, which would match the Latin form "Nero Caesar." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dsc/revelation-13.html; https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/why-is-the-number-of-the-beast-666/)
- **Symbolic/figurative interpretation (G.K. Beale / Reformed)**: numbers throughout Revelation are symbolic, not calculated by gematria. Triple six (666) is a contrast with divine sevens — it signifies **incompleteness and imperfection**. Seven = completeness; 666 = the "completeness of sinful incompleteness." The beast falls short of God's perfection. The triple six parodies the divine Trinity (three sevens = 777). (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/why-is-the-number-of-the-beast-666/)
- **"Number of a man"** (generic): without the article, "man" (ἀνθρώπου) means humanity in general — it is **fallen humanity's number**. Man was created on the sixth day but without entering God's seventh‑day rest, humanity is incomplete. The beast represents unregenerate humanity trying and failing to achieve divine likeness. (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/why-is-the-number-of-the-beast-666/)
- **Beale notes** that if gematria were intended, John would have alerted readers by saying "in Hebrew" or "in Greek" as he does elsewhere (9:11; 16:16). He does not. Likewise, 144,000 in the next chapter is symbolic of completeness of God's people — 666 contrasts as incompleteness of the beast's people. (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/why-is-the-number-of-the-beast-666/)
- **D.S. Clark** (StudyLight): As the beast is the Roman Empire, the man coordinated with the beast is the emperor. Nero's name in Hebrew (Neron Caesar) yields 666. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dsc/revelation-13.html)
- **Some early manuscripts have 616 instead of 666**. Irenaeus (late 2nd century) argued for 666 based on "the oldest and approved manuscripts." (https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/how-we-got-the-bible)
- **Gill**: The number consists of three Greek letters (χξϛ) numerically totaling 666. (https://www.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/13.htm)

## Where Protestant Traditions Differ

### The Beast: Future Individual vs. Historical/Systemic

- **Dispensational / Futurist (MacArthur / GTY, Guzik / Enduring Word, Precept Austin)**: The beast is a literal, future individual — the Antichrist — who will lead a revived Roman Empire, make a seven‑year covenant with Israel, break it after 3½ years, and persecute the saints. The rapture removes the church before this. The 42 months are the second half of the tribulation. (https://www.gty.org/sermons/66-44/the-beast-out-of-the-sea-part-1; https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-13/; https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
- **Historicist (Gill, some Reformed)**: The first beast represents the **Roman papacy** in its civil power; the second beast represents the papacy in its ecclesiastical power. The 42 months = 1,260 years of papal dominance. The mark is spiritual allegiance to Rome. The blasphemous names = papal titles. (https://www.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/13.htm)
- **Reformed / Idealist (Beale / Gospel Coalition)**: The beast represents **all oppressive, idolatrous state power throughout history** — not merely one future individual. The number 666 is symbolic of fallen humanity's incompleteness, not a gematria code for a specific person. The beast is "the supreme representative of unregenerate humanity." (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/why-is-the-number-of-the-beast-666/)
- **Preterist (implied in Ellicott, Pulpit)**: The beast imagery drew on Daniel to describe **contemporary Roman imperial persecution**. Nero (666 by gematria) was the immediate referent, though the vision may have continuing applications. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/13.htm; https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dsc/revelation-13.html)

### The Number 666

- **Gematria / Nero view** (older Protestant, some Baptists, general evangelical): 666 = the numerical value of "Neron Caesar" in Hebrew letters. This identifies the beast with Nero and, by extension, a future Nero‑like persecutor. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/dsc/revelation-13.html)
- **Symbolic / Trinity parody view** (Reformed, Beale): 666 is not for literal calculation but symbolizes imperfection contrasted with divine completeness (7). Triple six = parodic anti‑Trinity. (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/why-is-the-number-of-the-beast-666/)
- **Papal identification** (Historicist): Some historicists identified 666 with the Greek letters in "Lateinos" (Latin) or with the title "Vicarius Filii Dei." Gill does not press one specific calculation but identifies the beast with Rome. (https://www.biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/13.htm)

## Other Views

*(Note: I was unable to fetch Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Methodist/Wesleyan, or modern scholarship pages due to search/fetch limits. The notes below summarize what I was able to gather from the sources retrieved.)*

- **Catholic reading** (not directly retrieved): The search for Catholic interpretation at newadvent.org and catholic.com was attempted but could not be completed within the tool limits. Traditional Catholic exegesis often reads the beasts in light of Church history — some identifying the first beast with pagan Rome and the second with heresy or false religion, while affirming a future personal Antichrist before the Second Coming.
- **Modern scholarship** (bibleodyssey.org, netbible.org — not fetched): Based on the Beale article at The Gospel Coalition, modern scholarship often emphasizes the **symbolic and literary context** — the beast as a symbol of deified state power, using gematria to point to Nero but drawing on OT imagery (Daniel 7, Leviathan, etc.) for theological meaning rather than predictive timetable. (https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/why-is-the-number-of-the-beast-666/)
- **Early Church**: Irenaeus (late 2nd century) identified the first beast with Paul's "man of sin" (2 Thess. 2) and defended the 666 reading against the 616 variant. The early church did **not** identify Nero as the Beast — they expected a future fulfillment. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-13-commentary)
